StackType.rationale: PowerStackType.Counter. The sim has no StackType concept; Power.on_stack (powers.py:64-66) adds unconditionally, which is what PowerCmd.ModifyAmount does (PowerCmd.cs:236). Third-file citations, not hashed here.

DisplayAmount.rationale: PanachePower.cs:33 shows the CardsLeft counter instead of Amount in the UI. The sim keeps the two values apart the same way (`self.amount` is the damage, `self.cards_left` the counter, powers.py:3633) but has no display concept. Presentation.

InstanceType.issue: PanachePower.cs:35 declares PowerInstanceType.Instanced, so every Panache play is an independently-tracked instance with its own CardsLeft counter; the sim keeps one instance per power id (cmds.py:308) and a second play stacks the damage while sharing one counter. This is audits/seam/power_cmd.json's gap G5, which already names PanachePower among the 11 ported InstanceType powers; per binding rule 3 the same verdict, cross-referenced rather than re-argued. Unlike ToricToughness and TheBomb, Panache does NOT document the approximation or hand-roll a workaround. DORMANT: two simultaneous Panaches need two plays of a Rare colourless card in one combat. Named trigger: a second Panache play.

AfterCardPlayed.issue: The sim iterates `combat.enemies` filtered on `not enemy.is_gone` where C# uses CombatState.HittableEnemies, which additionally consults Hook.ShouldAllowHitting (Creature.cs:308-322). The sim therefore aims at creatures the game considers unhittable -- a mid-revival Illusion (powers.py:1572-1575) or a withered Decimillipede segment (powers.py:2354-2357). DORMANT: DamageCmd.deal re-checks should_allow_hitting at entry (cmds.py:51-52) and returns 0, so no damage lands; what still differs is that the command runs at all. Same finding as power/inferno's HittableEnemies guard, same verdict per binding rule 3. Named trigger: an unhittable-creature effect that depends on being targeted rather than damaged. Third-file citations, not hashed here.

AfterSideTurnEnd.issue: SLOT. AbstractModel.AfterSideTurnEnd is dispatched by Hook.AfterTurnEnd (Hook.cs:1267-1292), called for the player side at CombatManager.cs:1307 -- AFTER the turn-end card effects and the hand flush. The sim's on_player_turn_end is Hook.BeforeTurnEnd (combat.py:654), which runs BEFORE _process_turn_end_cards (combat.py:658) and before the flush (combat.py:661-662); the sim's real AfterTurnEnd slot, after_player_turn_end (combat.py:665), is available and unused. THE CONCRETE ROUTE, which applies to every unit in this group: StampedePower (powers.py:1025-1041) auto-plays Attack cards from ITS on_player_turn_end, i.e. inside the very same dispatch, and _process_turn_end_cards runs more card effects immediately after. So in the game every turn-end auto-play happens while this power is still on the creature, and in the sim whether it does depends on hook-registration order between this power and Stampede. Reproduce the affected population with `py audit/tools/power_census.py slots`. Third-file citations, not hashed here.

guards.rationale: Tautology in single-player; the sim omits it.

C# sets the flag on the FIRST AfterCardPlayed it sees and only starts counting on the second, so the Panache card play does not count towards itself; powers.py:3636,3641-3643 reproduces that exactly, including setting the flag on the way out rather than up front.
